cells.tense: The strength is here now, and the clearing is taking the false structure with it.
cells.act: keep following the star after everything that has happened
cells.ask: Take the version of your life you settled on a while back. Go on with it as it stands — no new proof asked for, nothing changed.
cells.core:
Something built on a wrong footing is coming down, and you're on your feet in the middle of it. When this is working, it looks like this: you don't rush to shore up what's failing, and you don't run from it either. You carry what's yours and you wait. The clearing is quick and you're slow about it on purpose, because the next move is already settled in you.

There's a version of your life you chose a while back. Not a plan you announce — just the way you kept walking. Go on with it exactly as it stands. No new proof, no fresh changes. It has been through worse than this. What's coming down was not what was holding you up.
cells.sheetLine: What's coming down was not what held you up.
cells.verb: holding on through what the body is being asked to carry
cells.place: where a false structure is coming down fast and the ground is not yet clear

cells.tense: You are bracing for a clearing that has not arrived yet.
cells.act: return the favour at its true size
cells.ask: Next time someone does something for you, give back only what it actually was — the meal, the hour, the favour itself. Not more.
cells.core:
You can hold through material pressure; under too much of that, you start clearing things out before any clearing comes — getting rid of what you own, bracing, pushing an ending sooner than it needs to arrive. It feels like strength. From where other people stand it looks like bracing, and it costs them, because you give past what anything asked for and then file it under steadiness.

The way back runs both directions at the same size. Next time someone does something for you, give back only what it actually was — the meal, the hour, the favour itself. Not more. You don't have to out-give anyone to be steady, and the returning can stop where the thing stopped. What comes down then comes down when it comes.
cells.sheetLine: You are clearing before the collapse and calling it strength.
cells.verb: holding on through what the body is being asked to carry
cells.place: where a false structure is coming down fast and the ground is not yet clear

cells.tense: You are still at a door that closed behind you, and it is closed.
cells.act: do the giving in the open this time, where it was always done unseen
cells.ask: Take some piece of what you do for someone that nobody sees, and do that piece in front of them. Just that piece, no announcement.
cells.core:
The clearing already happened, and you're standing where the structure used to be. You went through it holding what you carry, quietly, with nobody watching. That's the private kind of endurance: no witness, no acknowledgment, just the load and you. It works. It also runs down, and when it runs down you stop arriving in rooms you're already in.

Let one piece of what you do be seen by the person it's for. Take some piece of what you do for someone that nobody sees, and do that piece in front of them. Just that piece, no announcement and no explanation. Something was released when the false thing came down; this lets the same be said for what you kept holding.
cells.sheetLine: What you carried, nobody saw, and it is running down.
cells.verb: holding on through what the body is being asked to carry
cells.place: where a false structure is coming down fast and the ground is not yet clear

cells.tense: You are holding through this clearing and filing it under what happened to you.
cells.act: persist on hope that has been tested
cells.ask: Keep going with the hope you already carry, the one that has been through something. Hold it another week as your own choice, not the circumstance's.
cells.core:
Things built on a wrong footing fall away fast around you, and you stay upright, and your account of it is that it happened to you. Whatever came down came down. You kept on. You kept on because you could, and that keeping-on belongs to you, not to the circumstances. This is the part you leave out of the story you tell about your life.

The strength you show in a material grind is solid enough to be called chosen. Keep going with the hope you already carry, the one that has been through something. Hold it another week as your own choice, not the circumstance's. Then what got cleared has an author again.
cells.sheetLine: The ground cleared, but you are the one who kept on.

attempts.check: The draft risked saying the clearing is happening now, which the record does not establish — the seat names a rapid dissolution of what couldn't hold, not a timeline for this person's week. A reader could fairly say the collapse already happened and they're only standing in what's left. Each ask survives being wrong because it is diagnostic rather than predictive: following the chosen version another week, returning a favour at its true size, doing one unseen giving in the open, and naming a hope without a plan all teach the person something about what they have been carrying regardless of where the seat sits. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is any form of 'you are stronger than you know' — cut everywhere. Also cut the word 'collapse' as a promise about their life.
